sourceClaimMap.claim: explains that registered mortgages rank according to when they were lodged, and that the order can be changed by registering a mortgage priority form executed by every affected mortgagee
Changing priority is a formal land-title process, not an informal agreement between a borrower and broker.
the land registry for the property’s state or territory may require certain consents before it registers a dealing
the first loan’s own documents may restrict further security or require the first lender’s consent, whether or not the registry needs it

separates consents required for registration under the Real Property Act 1900 from consents that are not required for registration but may be needed to bind parties to a document’s terms, giving the example that a mortgagee may require consent under the terms of a mortgage
It also notes that a caveator’s consent is assumed to apply to all dealings.
That guidance covers NSW electronic lodgment only

In NSW electronic dealings, for example, the Registrar General separates consents required for registration from consents that may be needed to bind parties to a document’s terms, such as a mortgagee’s consent under a mortgage.
the first loan’s own documents may require the first lender’s consent before further security is granted, even where registration does not require it
A caveat is a notice of a claimed interest, not a registered mortgage

describes a caveat as a notice that generally prohibits registration of dealings affecting the claimed interest until it is withdrawn, removed, lapses or is cancelled, and says a caveat should not be seen as a viable alternative to registering the interest
The business.gov.au loan guide recommends comparing rates, charges, term and security requirements.
legal protections depend on loan purpose

commercial loans, including loans to small businesses, receive the lowest level of protection, and that lenders providing only commercial loans are not required to hold a credit licence or be members of the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA)
